title: Wren and the Wolf
premise: In the city of Vell, where magic is outlawed and memory is currency, Ulyana Pemberton survives by stealing recollections from the wealthy and selling them as charms. When the crown's witch-hunt sweeps the city, she discovers that her own stolen memories hold fragments of a soul — her brother's — sold years ago to the court beneath the mountain, where it burns as fuel for the last dragon-fire. To reclaim him before the fire gutters out and takes his soul with it, she must ally with a disgraced inquisitor, a dragon-priestess, and the very thieves' guild that once betrayed her. In the end, Ulyana frees her brother's soul by feeding the fire her own most precious memory instead, choosing belonging with the living over the past she cannot restore.
about_author: Dominic Villalobos is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated letters in a mountain province before turning to fiction. He writes fantasy about people who survive institutions by bending them.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She sells a widow a bottled memory of her dead husband, showing both her gift and her guilt. Establishes Vell's fear of magic and Ulyana's loneliness. Emotional beat: quiet complicity — she profits from grief while hiding in plain sight.

chapters.title: Ash on the Proclamation Board
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The crown posts a hunt for the gifted; a neighbor is dragged away screaming. Ulyana burns her stock but keeps one charm she cannot explain: a memory that isn't hers, of a boy at a mountain gate. Beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: What the Thief Forgot
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, dreamlike flashback. Under a sleepless night, the foreign memory surfaces: her brother Tomas, sold to the court beneath the mountain to feed the dragon-fire. She realizes she stole this memory from herself to survive. Beat: devastating recognition.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor Who Quit
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Corvin Ashe, a former witch-hunter who resigned after burning an innocent. Ulyana blackmails him for knowledge of the mountain court; he agrees to guide her for reasons he won't name. Beat: wary, transactional alliance.

chapters.title: Guild Debts
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She returns to the thieves' guild that exiled her three years ago to buy passage; its master, Sable, demands she steal the guild's seized ledger back from the crown as payment. Beat: humiliation laced with old belonging.

chapters.title: The Ledger Job
chapters.summary: Dual POV, Ulyana and Corvin. A tense heist through the Hall of Records; they succeed but Corvin sees her use magic openly and says nothing. The ledger reveals the mountain court buys souls from the crown directly. Beat: trust tentatively forming.

chapters.title: Sable's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Sable betrays her to the hunters to save the guild, revealing he knew about Tomas all along and took a cut. Ulyana escapes with Corvin's help but the city gates close behind them. Beat: betrayal confirming her isolation.

chapters.title: The Road Beneath
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. On the mountain road, Corvin confesses the innocent he burned was a memory-thief like Ulyana. They argue about justice outside the law; neither wins. Beat: two broken people finding an uneasy moral common ground.

chapters.title: Priestess of the Guttering Flame
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. They reach the shrine of Ysolde, last dragon-priestess, who tends the dying fire from afar. Ysolde reveals the truth: the court feeds souls to the dragon-fire to keep the mountain's wards alive — and the fire has weeks left. Beat: awe curdling into horror.

chapters.title: The Court of Salt and Smoke
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Disguised as a soul-broker, Ulyana infiltrates the underground court and sees the vaults of bottled souls, including one labeled Pemberton. Beat: cold fury beneath a mask of commerce.

chapters.title: A Soul on the Shelf
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She reaches Tomas's vessel but touching it triggers a ward; she glimpses his living memory inside — he chose to be sold to pay her debts. Beat: guilt transformed into fierce resolve.

chapters.title: The Warden's Price
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. Captured by the court's warden, Corvin is offered reinstatement if he denounces Ulyana. He stalls, buying time, and learns the warden plans to let the fire die and hoard the remaining souls as power. Beat: temptation resisted.

chapters.title: Smoke and Mirrors
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Using her gift, Ulyana steals a memory from the warden himself and discovers the fire doesn't need souls at all — the court invented the ritual to monopolize magic. Beat: revelation that reframes everything.

chapters.title: Ysolde's Choice
chapters.summary: Ysolde's POV. The priestess reveals the fire can be fed by any freely given memory, but the giver forgets what they give forever. She offers to take the burden herself; Ulyana refuses to let another pay. Beat: sacrifice offered and contested.

chapters.title: The Breaking of Corvin Ashe
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. Tortured for Ulyana's location, Corvin breaks — not by betraying her, but by unleashing the suppressed magic he never admitted having. Beat: self-destruction as liberation.

chapters.title: Riot in the Vaults
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. Corvin's escape ignites chaos; bottled souls begin waking as the wards fail; Ulyana fights toward Tomas's vessel through collapsing corridors. Beat: escalating momentum, everything on the line.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon-Fire
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. At the fire's heart, the warden offers Ulyana a trade: Tomas's soul for the ledger naming every gifted citizen in Vell. Beat: the corrupt bargain laid bare — power versus blood.

chapters.title: What Ulyana Gives
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, climax. She refuses the trade, shatters the ledger, and feeds the fire her own treasured memory — three stolen years of small charms and the widow's gratitude — not Tomas's sale, but her life since. The fire roars back to life, freed from souls. Beat: costly, liberating sacrifice.

chapters.title: Ash and Aftermath
chapters.summary: Corvin's POV. The court collapses; the warden drowns in his own hoarded souls; Tomas wakes human and whole. Ulyana remembers nothing of why she came. Beat: victory shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: The Brother She Doesn't Know
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas recognizes Ulyana though she can't place him; he chooses not to force the memory back on her, instead simply staying near. Beat: tender, aching reconnection without restoration.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Back in Vell, the hunt collapses as the ledger's destruction leaves the crown powerless; the guild fractures and Sable falls. Ulyana opens a new stall selling honest charms — no stolen memories. Beat: earned peace, changed terms.

chapters.title: Wren and the Wolf
chapters.summary: Final chapter, alternating Ulyana and Tomas. On the anniversary, Tomas gives Ulyana a charm containing one returned fragment: the boy at the mountain gate. She doesn't understand it fully, but she keeps it. Beat: belonging found not in recovered pasts, but in chosen company.
